what_its_for: Nicardipine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and chest pain (angina). It works by relaxing and widening your blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard and blood can flow more easily through your body.
how_to_take: Take nicardipine exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow the capsules whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food, but try to take it the same way each time. If you are taking the extended-release (SR) capsules, do NOT crush, chew, or open them. Take your doses at the same times every day to keep a steady level of the medicine in your body.
dosing: Your doctor will choose the right dose for you based on your condition and how you respond to treatment. A typical starting dose for regular capsules is 20 mg taken three times a day (every 8 hours). For extended-release capsules, the usual starting dose is 30 mg taken twice a day (every 12 hours). Your doctor may slowly increase your dose over time. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and just take the next one at your regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one, as this could cause your blood pressure to drop too low and make you feel dizzy or faint.
storage: Store nicardipine capsules at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the medication away from light, heat, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication after the expiration date printed on the label. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused medication.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking grapefruit juice or eating grapefruit while taking nicardipine, as it can increase the amount of medicine in your blood and cause unwanted side effects. Avoid standing up too quickly from a sitting or lying position, as nicardipine can cause dizziness, especially when you first start taking it. Be careful with alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure further and increase dizziness. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: chest pain that gets worse or does not go away, severe dizziness or fainting, rapid or irregular heartbeat, sudden swelling of your hands, feet, or ankles, shortness of breath, severe headache, or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, or swelling of the face, lips, or throat. Also call your doctor if your blood pressure readings at home seem too high or too low, or if you feel your symptoms are getting worse.
when_it_works: You may start to notice a lowering of your blood pressure within the first 1 to 2 hours after taking nicardipine. However, it may take 1 to 2 weeks of regular use before you feel the full benefit of the medication. Even if you feel well, keep taking it as prescribed. High blood pressure often has no symptoms, so do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Older adults (over 65): You may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering effects and may be at higher risk for dizziness and falls. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose and increase it slowly. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as nicardipine may not be safe to use during pregnancy and it may pass into breast milk. Kidney or liver problems: If you have kidney or liver disease, your doctor may need to adjust your dose, as these organs help process the medication. Children: Nicardipine is not commonly used in children, and dosing would be determined by a specialist.
